MA No. 823/2009 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company seeking total exoneration from its liability to pay compensation to the claimants.
2. MA No. 1006/2009 has been preferred by the claimants on the ground of inadequacy of compensation, seeking enhancement of the compensation amount.

3. The facts of both the appeals are identical and arise out of a common award dated 07.05.2009 passed by the First Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to the Court of First Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.), in Claim NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:260 2 MA-823-2009 Case No. 124/2008.

sentences.text:
1 4. Brief facts of the case are that the claimants filed a claim petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, asserting that on 04.07.2006 the deceased, Banti @
Khemraj Singh, was travelling from Jaipur to Baduke along with goods relating to a tower in Jeep No. RJ-14-G-0153, which was being driven by the driver of the offending vehicle.

When the jeep reached near the petrol pump under Police Station Machhipura on the Jaipur-Baduke turn, the driver, while driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, overturned it, as a result of which the deceased came under the jeep and sustained grievous injuries.
The injured was taken to Parwatsar Hospital, District Nagaur, by persons present at the spot, where he succumbed to the injuries during treatment.
The incident was reported to the police, an FIR was registered, and thereafter a charge-sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. Thereafter, the Insurance Company filed its written statement before the Claims Tribunal,
contending that at the time of the accident the deceased was travelling in a goods/commercial vehicle in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and, therefore, the Insurance Company was not liable to pay any compensation to the claimants.
The driver and owner of the offending vehicle did not file their written statements and were accordingly proceeded ex parte.

6. The Claims Tribunal, after framing the issues and appreciating the evidence on record, allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs. 4,41,500/- , directing the appellant-Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimants with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:260 3 MA-823-2009 offending vehicle.
7. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that the award passed by the Claims Tribunal is contrary to law.

It was contended that at the time of the accident, as many as five persons were travelling in the jeep, whereas its seating capacity was only three persons, which amounted to a clear breach of the insurance policy.
It was further submitted that the Tribunal failed to consider the testimony of Punit (DW-1), who deposed that the vehicle was being driven in violation of the policy conditions.
Though the Tribunal recorded a finding regarding breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, it committed an error in directing the Insurance Company to pay and recover.
Hence, it was prayed that the Insurance Company be totally exonerated from liability.

8. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants sought enhancement of the compensation amount and submitted that the Claims Tribunal committed an error in not awarding compensation under the heads of future prospects and consortium.

It was further submitted that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle as a representative of the goods and, therefore, there was no breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence, it was prayed that the appeal filed by the Insurance Company be dismissed and the compensation amount be enhanced.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
10.

The Insurance Company has preferred the present appeal on the ground that at the time of the accident the deceased was travelling in the commercial vehicle as a fare-paying passenger and not as I.C.I.C.I.Lumbard General Insurance ... vs Smt.Chandrakala Chouhan on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184294732/
2 a representative of the goods.

entities.text: I.C.I.C.I.Lumbard General Insurance ... vs Smt.Chandrakala Chouhan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:260 4 MA-823-2009 11.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the deceased was working as a contractor with RKS Enterprise Tally (Communication and Construction Group) and relied upon the identity card marked as Ex. P/10.
12.

Upon consideration of the evidence of the claimants and the brother of the deceased, it is clear that the claimants failed to adduce any cogent or reliable evidence to establish that the deceased was travelling with goods as an authorized representative.
The evidence on record clearly indicates that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle after paying rent/fare.
Thus, the deceased was an unauthorized passenger in a commercial vehicle, which amounts to a clear violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The Insurance Company had not received any premium for carrying passengers in the offending vehicle.
Consequently, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the claimants.

14. This Court is of the considered view that the Claims Tribunal committed an error in directing the Insurance Company to pay compensation with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, the said finding is modified, and the Insurance Company is totally exonerated from liability.
The owner and driver of the offending vehicle are directed to pay the compensation to the claimants jointly and severally.
15. Accordingly, MA No. 823/2009 stands disposed of.

16. So far as MA No. 1006/2009 filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation is concerned, it is found that the Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs. 3,000/- per month, which is just and proper.

17. With regard to loss of income including future prospects, in light of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:260 5 MA-823-2009 judgment of the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled to an addition of 40% towards future prospects.

sentences.text: Further, as per the decision in Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121 , the appropriate multiplier is 17, with one-third deduction towards personal expenses.

sentences.text: Claimant Nos. 1 and 5 are also entitled to compensation under the head of consortium.

18. Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to compensation under the following heads:
Income: Rs. 3,000  12 = Rs. 36,000/- per annum Future prospects @ 40% Rs.
14,400/-

Total income: Rs. 50,400/-
Dependency (2/3)= Rs. 33,600/- Multiplier: 17 Loss of dependency: Rs. 33,600  17 = Rs. 5,71,200/- Loss of consortium (Rs. 40,000  2)= Rs. 80,000/- Loss of estate and funeral expenses: Rs. 30,000/-
I.C.I.C.I.Lumbard General Insurance ... vs Smt.Chandrakala Chouhan on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184294732/
3

Total compensation: Rs. 6,81,200/-
19.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the present case is Rs. 6,81,200/- as against the award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs. 4,41,500/-.
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs. 2,39,700/- over and above the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
20. In the result, MA No. 1006/2009 filed by the claimants is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation by Rs. 2,39,700/-.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate fixed by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization and shall be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.
21. Both the miscellaneous appeals stand disposed of in the above terms.
